results.question: how long do i keep tax records
results.answer:
You should keep your tax records for the length of time required by the Internal Revenue Code, which is generally the period of limitations for the tax return on which they are needed.  

According to the IRS Publication 583 (Starting a Business):

> “You must keep your records as long as they may be needed for the administration of any provision of the Internal Revenue Code. Generally, this means you must keep records that support an item of income or deduction on a return until the period of limitations for that return runs out.” [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16)  

> “Employment taxes. If you have employees, you must keep all employment tax records for at least 4 years after the date the tax becomes due or is paid, whichever is later.” [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16)  

> “Assets. Keep records relating to property until the period of limitations expires for the year in which you dispose of the property in a taxable disposition.” [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16)  

> “When your records are no longer needed for tax purposes, do not discard them until you check to see if you have to keep them longer for other purposes.” [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16)  

So, in practice:

| Record type | Required retention period | Source |
|-------------|---------------------------|--------|
| Income or deduction records that support a tax return | Until the period of limitations expires for that return (generally 3‑6 years, depending on the situation) | [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16) |
| Employment tax records | At least 4 years after the tax becomes due or is paid | [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16) |
| Asset‑related records (e.g., depreciation, basis) | Until the period of limitations expires for the year in which the asset is disposed of | [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16) |

If other non‑tax purposes require the records (e.g., insurance or creditors), retain them as long as those parties require them.



**Sources:**
1. [irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf (Page 16)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/318-irs_publication_583_starting_a_business.pdf#page=16)

results.question: how many employees before ada employment rules apply
results.answer:
A business must have **15 or more employees** before the ADA employment provisions require compliance.  
[[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/316-ada_guide_small_business.pdf#page=19)



**Sources:**
1. [ada_guide_small_business.pdf (Page 19)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/316-ada_guide_small_business.pdf#page=19)

results.question: what forms do i keep for injuries and how long do i keep them
results.answer:
For a small business, OSHA requires you to keep the following injury‑ and illness‑recording forms:

| Form | What it records | How long you must keep it |
|------|-----------------|---------------------------|
| **OSHA Form 300** – Log of Work‑Related Injuries and Illnesses | Primary log of all occupational injuries and illnesses (except minor first‑aid cases) | At least **five years** (office or worksite) |
| **OSHA Form 301** – Injury and Illness Incident Report | Detailed supplementary record for every recordable injury or illness | At least **five years** (office or worksite) |
| **OSHA Form 300A** – Summary of Work‑Related Injuries and Illnesses | Annual summary that aggregates the Form 300/301 data | At least **five years** (office or worksite) |

* Source (forms themselves are described on page 14 of the handbook):  
  - `"Occupational injuries or illnesses, except minor injuries requiring only first aid, are recorded on OSHA Form 300 (Log of Work‑Related Injuries and Illnesses)."` [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/319-osha_small_business_handbook.pdf#page=14)  
  - `"A supplementary record of each recordable occupational injury and illness is prepared for recordable cases on OSHA Form 301 (Injury and Illness Incident Report)."` [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/319-osha_small_business_handbook.pdf#page=14)  
  - `"An annual summary is prepared at the end of each calendar year using OSHA Form 300A (Summary of Work‑Related Injuries and Illnesses)."` [[1]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/319-osha_small_business_handbook.pdf#page=14)

* Source (retention period):  
  - `"Injury and illness records (OSHA 300, 300A, and 301) are kept at the worksite for at least five years."` [[2]](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/319-osha_small_business_handbook.pdf#page=15)

These are the only documents explicitly required for injury recordkeeping in the handbook; no other forms are prescribed for this purpose.



**Sources:**
1. [osha_small_business_handbook.pdf (Page 14)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/319-osha_small_business_handbook.pdf#page=14)
2. [osha_small_business_handbook.pdf (Page 15)](https://storage.googleapis.com/docsynth-fbb02.appspot.com/workspaces/4219/319-osha_small_business_handbook.pdf#page=15)
